title: Epaulette mate
line: The king's own rooks on either side block it in.

steps.text: Epaulette mate: the king's own pieces sit on both sides of it, like the epaulettes on a uniform. A queen check from the front is enough.
Tap the two black pieces that block their own king's way to the sides.
steps.hint: Look along the back rank, right beside the king.
steps.after: Both rooks. The king can only flee forward, and the queen will take those squares.

steps.text: Mate with the queen, two squares in front of the king.
steps.hint: The queen goes along the diagonal to the king's file.
steps.after: Epaulette mate. The queen takes the three squares in front of the king, and the rooks block the two beside it.

steps.text: Now you are Black in the same position, and the queen threatens mate on d6. Unbox your king first.

wrong.a7a6: Then the queen comes to d6, and it is mate.
wrong.h7h6: Then the queen comes to d6, and it is mate.
wrong.g7g6: Then the queen comes to d6, and it is mate.
wrong.b7b6: Then the queen comes to d6, and it is mate.
wrong.d8d7: That gets the king out, but it stands in the open, and the queen checks it again from d3 at once.

steps.hint: Move the king off the back rank, or move a rook so the king has a square beside it.
steps.after: The box is open. A check on d6 is no longer mate.

summary: A king squeezed between its own pieces can be mated by a single check from the front. Leave it a square.
